definition: The cosmic order, truth and rightness that sustain the world and that Ahura Mazda embodies. Zoroastrians uphold asha in good thoughts, good words and good deeds; its opposite is druj, the lie.
Deceit, disorder and the lie, the moral power of Angra Mainyu and the opposite of asha. In the Gathas, choosing druj means choosing destruction rather than life.
The 'holy immortal ones', divine beings who personify the attributes of Ahura Mazda, such as Good Mind, Truth and Dominion. Later tradition counts six, with Ahura Mazda at their head.
Seventeen hymns in the Yasna, the oldest part of the Avesta and the core of Zoroastrian liturgy. They are attributed to Zarathushtra and composed in an archaic Iranian dialect.
The corpus of Zoroastrian sacred texts composed in the Avestan language, including the Yasna, Vendidad and Yashts. Only a portion of the tradition survives.
Ferdowsi's Persian epic, the Book of Kings, completed around 1010 CE. It retells Iran's legendary history and is the main source for Rostam, Zal, Kaveh and Zahhak.
The final renovation of the world at the end of time, when evil is defeated, the dead are raised and creation is restored to its original goodness.
A future saviour figure who helps bring about the frashokereti. Later Zoroastrian tradition speaks of several saoshyants, born from the prophet's line.
A winged symbol with a human figure, common in Zoroastrian art and widely used today as an emblem of the faith. Its original meaning is debated by scholars.
The underground enclosure that Yima builds at Ahura Mazda's command in the Vendidad, stocked with pairs of every species so that life survives a catastrophic winter.
